messages.subject: Re: haploids; cM positions
parts:
>
> 1) Can Rqtl be used with haploid data?
> Toxoplasma has a haploid genome so even though we know these are crosses they will never have heterozygous alleles. When I input them into my starting file I labeled them as AA and BB but when I gave them to R it insisted that the BB were all in fact AB
>
> toxo <- read.cross("csvr", file="/Users/Andrea/Documents/Lab Work/Rqtl/sortedSNPsearly.csv", genotypes =c("A", "B"), na.strings = "-", alleles =c("A", "B"))

Follow that with

class(toxo)[1] <- "haploid"

or use crosstype="haploid" in the call to read.cross:

toxo <- read.cross("csvr", file="/Users/Andrea/Documents/Lab Work/Rqtl/sortedSNPsearly.csv",
genotypes =c("A", "B"), na.strings = "-", alleles =c("A", "B"), crosstype="haploid")


> 2) Do I need to have marker ID's on my SNPs? None of them are named since they are just SNPs called from whole genome sequencing. Additionally, do the SNPs have to be in cM to work, I converted them but I would rather keep them in Mb (from bp) if that is cool with "qtl"

If you have very dense markers (very few recombination events between any two markers), it won't matter.

But if you have sufficient sample size, you can estimate the cM positions from the data:

gmap <- est.map(toxo)
toxo <- replace.map(toxo, gmap)

karl
